best_for: Windows users who miss the Mac's spacebar preview, or anyone who opens files only to check what is inside them.
description:
QuickLook is a file previewer for Windows, built as a community project under the QL-Win name on GitHub. The point is to save you the wait of launching a full program just to see what a file holds.

Beyond the usual photos and documents, it shows Photoshop and Illustrator files, e-books in EPUB and MOBI, comics in CBZ and CBR, rendered Markdown, subtitles, and a hex view of binary files. In the preview, Enter opens the file in its normal app, the mouse wheel zooms images, Ctrl plus the wheel zooms PDFs, and dragging spins a 3D model. You can drag the file straight out of the preview. It also works in Total Commander and xplorer², and in OneDrive and Dropbox folders.

points.title: Press Space to peek
points.text: Select a file in File Explorer and press Space to see it in a preview window. Space or Esc closes it, and the arrow keys step to the next file. The app waits in the system tray.

points.title: Office and CAD need plugins
points.text: Images, video, audio, code, archives, fonts and 3D models preview out of the box. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, CAD drawings and PostScript need plugins such as OfficeViewer or CADImport, which you install by previewing a .qlplugin file and restarting.

points.title: Store build or installer
points.text: The Microsoft Store version updates itself but has limited support inside Open and Save dialogs. The installer gives the full feature set, and the project also offers a portable build and a Scoop package.

points.title: Little data leaves your PC
points.text: The privacy policy says the app collects no personal information and only talks to GitHub's releases service. It is free and open source under GPL-3.0.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version, which makes sense since macOS has Quick Look built in.

points.title: Installs without admin rights
points.text: The installer listed here is a 32-bit MSI that installs for the current user only, which suits work PCs where you lack administrator rights. The Windows listing keeps 15 versions.
